analysis.title: Trex Company Inc. (TREX) 3Q26 Recap: Self-Help Efforts Along with Exposure to Secular Shift and Faster Growing Outdoor Living Suggest Upside to 2027 EPS
key_insights: Goldman maintains Buy on TREX and raises its 12-month price target to $69 from $61, based on 18.0x (was 17.0x) its Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA estimate. The higher multiple reflects increased confidence in delivery on strategic initiatives.

3Q26 sales grew 26%. About 11pts or $30mn came from load-in tied to the shift in distribution and about 15% from higher volumes. That is about 900bps above the decking industry, up about 6%, while composites rose about 9%.
Management said industry decking sell-out was up 6% while TREX was up in the teens, which GS reads as true demand rather than pull forward. Adjusted sell-in and sell-out both grew in the teens.

Channel inventories were flat y/y in 3Q despite the $30mn load-in. SBP is running below key partners' year-ago levels, which GS partly attributes to macro uncertainty and the industry's disciplined approach to the distribution shifts.
Attachment rates for railing, fasteners and accessories are about 30%, up from the mid-20% range at the start of the year. Railing is up about 500bps YTD and up double-digits.
Initial traction in converting regional dealers validates the $100mn opportunity, and Little Rock is on track to be 50% operational by year-end.

GS's 2027 estimate is now built on sell-out up 6%, creating a clearer path to the targeted $2bn of sales in 2030. Growth levers are share gains from tertiary brands and a full PVC decking assortment rolling out in 2027, where Trex is under-penetrated.

Near-term gross margin headwinds: elevated diesel prices were a $4mn or about 130bps drag, plus higher depreciation and Little Rock start-up costs. Start-up pressure continues into early 2027, and management expects Little Rock to reach parity with legacy assets by 2Q.
The 4Q gross margin guide of 34-35% implies about 430bps of y/y expansion at the midpoint. GS models 4Q sales up 12.0% y/y, at the high end of guidance.

GS's 2027 adj. EBITDA margin forecast is 28.1%, up 54bps y/y, using SG&A/sales of 17.5%. GS says this could be conservative. Trex reaffirmed its long-term guide of about 100bps of gross margin expansion per $100mn of incremental revenue.
Capex is moderating as the Arkansas investment winds down. GS forecasts $226mn of free cash flow in 2027, supporting M&A, and $303mn of buybacks.

The stock rose 14% on the day of the report. GS sees the current valuation as an attractive entry point and expects a re-rating over time from volume growth, a structural low-cost advantage and expanding ROIC.
GS scenario analysis: the 12-month upside case implies $84 (39.0x 2027 EPS) and the downside case implies $49 (26.0x 2027 EPS). GS sees favorable risk/reward at the current $50.00 price.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised to $69 from $61 on an 18.0x multiple (was 17.0x) of Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA. GS cites a commercial and operational turnaround, share gains and Little Rock ramp, and sees 38% upside from $50.00.

sector_views.rationale: Secular shift from wood to composites, faster growth in outdoor living, and elevated mortgage rates making R&R more attractive than moving.

earnings_insights: TREX 3Q26 reported sales growth +26% y/y (reported, per management on the call), including about $30mn of distribution load-in.
GS 2026E adj. EPS (estimate) raised to $1.88 from $1.80. 2027E to $2.02 from $2.00 and 2028E to $2.42 from $2.30. These are GS estimates, not reported figures.

GS 2026E revenue estimate is $1,301.4mn (was $1,244.3mn). 2027E is $1,350.0mn (was $1,301.8mn), which implies 3.7% y/y growth including the impact of the $35mn load-in this year. 2028E is $1,420.2mn (was $1,366.9mn).

4Q26 company guide (as cited by GS): gross margin 34-35%, about 430bps y/y expansion at the midpoint. GS estimate is 4Q sales up 12.0% y/y, at the high end of the guide. GS 4Q26E EPS is $0.12 per the key data table.
GS 2027E adj. EBITDA margin is 28.1% (estimate), up 54bps y/y. GS 2027E FCF is $226mn and buybacks are $303mn (estimates).
Trex management targets $2bn of sales by 2030 and reaffirmed about 100bps of gross margin expansion per $100mn of incremental revenue.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Underlying industry demand was steady this summer. TREX grew in the teens, about 900bps above the market.
Composites are outgrowing the broader decking industry, consistent with the shift away from wood.
GS's 2027 estimate is now built on industry sell-out growth of 6%.

trade_ideas.description: Buy TREX (12-month price target $69, 38% upside from $50.00)
trade_ideas.rationale: Self-help initiatives, share gains from the composites shift and faster-growing outdoor living support upside to 2027 EPS.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker consumer confidence limiting R&R spending, delays in strategic initiatives, higher raw material costs not passed through, loss of a key customer or distributor.

risk_factors: Decline in consumer confidence limiting willingness to spend on R&R projects, especially larger-ticket items.
Delays or inability to deliver on strategic initiatives.
Increase in raw material costs and inability to pass them through.
Loss of a key customer or distributor could impact sales.
Elevated diesel fuel prices, higher depreciation and Little Rock start-up costs pressure near-term gross margin.
